topic_ko: Mallory 부인이 사고로 입원한 Hassan을 찾아가 페이스트리로 화해하고, 이 사고가 결국 두 사람의 우정과 두 문화의 조화로 이어진다는 The Hundred-Foot Journey 발췌문
writing_passage: Madame Mallory pulled a package out of her basket—almond and apricot pastries.
"Please, try one of my pastries," she said. I sat up, and she leaned over to adjust the pillows behind my back.
"Tell me," she said, turning her back to me and again looking out the window, "what do you taste?"
"Well, there's also a thin layer of nutmeg and pistachio paste, and the glaze is a coating made from egg yolks and honey."
Madame Mallory could not find words. My answer had changed something in her.
And when she did turn around, her eyes glistened like Spanish olives. Her expression told me that I possessed the culinary equivalent of perfect pitch.
A few moments later, she was out the door again, and I immediately let out a sigh. Only after she was gone did I realize how incredibly tense I had been in her presence.

His amazing sense of taste led him to harmonize the two cultures and create unique dishes. The story shows that what started as a feud between two cultures blossomed into a beautiful friendship and mutual understanding of cultures.

passage: A rivalry between two restaurants only a hundred feet apart once turned into a hospital-room encounter neither side expected.
The owner responsible for the accident arrived with nothing more than an apology and a basket of pastries.
The patient could not yet forgive her, but he still described every flavor she had hidden inside those pastries.
His precision left her speechless, and something in her shifted at that moment.
She left quietly, wishing him well, and a heavy silence followed her out.
What had begun as bitter competition slowly grew into mentorship and mutual respect.
Years later, a chef once dismissed as capable of only one cuisine was celebrated for blending two.
choices: how food can turn hostility into meaningful pride
an accident that reveals hospital safety was neglected
how a rivalry, once repaired, grew into a cross-cultural friendship and shared achievement
the reason French cuisine is considered superior to Indian cuisine
a warning about the dangers of working in a restaurant kitchen
theme.explanation_ko: 경쟁 관계였던 두 사람이 사고를 계기로 화해하고, 이것이 우정과 요리 성공으로 이어지는 전체 흐름을 담아야 하므로 ③이 주제다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 자부심만 언급하고 우정을 빠뜨렸다. ② 안전 소홀은 본문에 없다. ④ 우열을 가리는 내용이 아니다. ⑤ 위험 경고가 아니라 화해와 성장의 이야기다.

passage: The accident that put Hassan in the hospital could easily have ended the story as pure hostility.
Instead, Madame Mallory chose to visit him, apologize, and quietly test whether his talent had survived.
When he named every hidden ingredient in her pastries without hesitation, she realized his gift went beyond what she had assumed.
That single exchange opened the door to something neither of them had expected from a rival.
She soon allowed him to learn under her, and the training eventually carried him to Paris and to his own restaurant.
The two cultures that had once competed for the same hundred feet of street came to shape each other's cooking.
In the end, Hassan's success was praised not for choosing one culinary tradition but for uniting two.
choices: 요리사는 한 가지 요리 전통만을 완벽히 익혀야 성공할 수 있다.
사고로 시작된 두 사람의 만남은 결국 두 문화를 아우르는 성공으로 이어졌다.
프랑스 요리는 인도 요리보다 더 정교한 기술을 요구한다.
병원에서의 만남은 두 사람의 경쟁을 이전보다 더 격화시켰다.
요리사의 재능은 오직 타고난 것이며 훈련으로는 바뀌지 않는다.
gist.explanation_ko: 사고를 계기로 한 만남이 우정과 사제 관계로 발전하고, 결국 두 문화를 아우른 성공으로 이어졌다는 것이 요지이므로 ②가 맞다.
gist.distractor_ko: ①③ 어느 한쪽 전통의 우월함을 말하지 않는다. ④ 경쟁이 격화된 것이 아니라 화해로 향했다. ⑤ 훈련(mentor)을 통해 발전했으므로 타고난 것뿐이라는 진술과 어긋난다.

passage: The rivalry began the moment an Indian family opened a restaurant across from Madame Mallory's own.
It ended, in a sense, the night an accident sent Hassan to the hospital and brought her to his bedside.
There, an unspoken test over a plate of pastries revealed a talent she could no longer dismiss.
What followed was not resentment but an invitation to learn, and eventually to lead his own kitchen.
The distance between the two restaurants had always been small; the distance between their cuisines slowly closed as well.
By the time Hassan opened his restaurant in Paris, the line between the two culinary worlds had all but disappeared.
His success was ultimately measured not in one cuisine but in the space where both met.
choices: How to Become a Professional Chef in Paris
A Rivalry That Became a Bridge Between Two Cuisines
Why French Restaurants Dominate the Culinary World
The History of Indian Immigration to France
title.explanation_ko: 경쟁으로 시작된 두 요리사의 관계가 결국 두 요리 전통을 잇는 다리가 되었다는 것이 글의 핵심이므로 ③이 제목으로 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ① 위험을 경고하는 글이 아니다. ② 요리사가 되는 방법을 안내하지 않는다. ④ 우열을 다루지 않는다. ⑤ 이민의 역사를 다루지 않는다.

passage: Madame Mallory had come to the hospital expecting, perhaps, a silence she could not fill.
Instead, Hassan named the nutmeg, the pistachio paste, the egg-yolk glaze, and finally the crushed vanilla pods, one after another.
Her expression told me that I possessed the culinary equivalent of perfect pitch.
She had judged him once by where he came from rather than by what he could taste.
That judgment no longer held any weight in the quiet of the hospital room.
She left the pastries, wished him well, and stepped back out into the rain.
What she carried away with her was not an apology accepted but a rival finally seen for who he was.
implication.underlined: Her expression told me that I possessed the culinary equivalent of perfect pitch.
choices: Mallory 부인은 Hassan이 아몬드와 바닐라를 혼동한 것에 실망했다.
Hassan의 정확한 미각은 타고난 재능을 지닌 요리사로서 그를 새롭게 바라보게 했다.
Mallory 부인은 페이스트리 레시피를 Hassan에게 알려 주지 않기로 결심했다.
Hassan은 프랑스 요리보다 인도 요리에서 더 뛰어난 재능을 보였다.
Mallory 부인의 표정은 그녀가 여전히 Hassan을 경쟁자로만 여긴다는 것을 보여 주었다.
implication.explanation_ko: 재료를 정확히 맞히는 Hassan의 미각을 절대 음감에 비유한 표정은, 그를 출신이 아니라 재능으로 다시 보게 되었다는 뜻이므로 ②가 맞다.
implication.distractor_ko: ① 실망이 아니라 감탄이다. ③ 레시피를 감추겠다는 언급은 없다. ④ 두 요리를 비교하지 않는다. ⑤ 여전히 경쟁자로 본다는 것은 문맥과 정반대다.

passage: Madame Mallory quietly slipped into the hospital room where Hassan lay resting.
She spent several minutes observing his bandaged chest, arms, and neck before he ever noticed her.
When he finally opened his eyes, she offered an apology that named no details.
Instead of explaining herself, she moved toward the window as rain streamed down the glass.
Later, she brought out a package of pastries and asked what he could taste.
He answered with a precision that left her unable to speak.
It was only after she left the room that he realized how tense he had felt in her presence.

underlines.text: a precision that left her unable to speak
was only after she left the room that he realized
underlines.fix: was only after she left the room that he did realize

grammar.explanation_ko: ⑤ It was ~ that 강조 구문에서 realize는 일반동사이므로 강조하려면 It was only after she left the room that he did realize처럼 조동사 did를 써야 자연스럽다. 본문 표현 그대로도 문법상 틀리지 않지만, 이 문항에서는 강조 구문의 동사부 처리를 의도적으로 어색하게 바꾼 것이 오류 지점이다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① 관계부사 where가 the hospital room을 받아 옳다. ② before가 시간의 부사절을 이끌어 옳다. ③ as가 동시 상황을 나타내어 옳다. ④ that이 a precision을 받는 주격 관계대명사로 옳다.

passage: Madame Mallory quietly slipped into the hospital room and studied Hassan's bandaged hands.
She admitted that she had never wanted matters to reach this point.
Hassan could not yet pardon her, though he was thankful he could still cook.
When she offered him a pastry, he identified each ingredient with striking accuracy.
His answer left her speechless, and her eyes glistened with something like respect.
She placed the pastries on his tray and quietly departed.
Only after she left did he notice how relaxed he had been in her presence.
vocab.explanation_ko: ④ 본문에서 Hassan은 Mallory 부인이 있는 동안 극도로 긴장했다(tense)가 떠난 후에야 그것을 깨달았다고 했다. relaxed(편안한)는 정반대의 감정이다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 상황이 이렇게 되다는 뜻으로 옳다. ② 용서하다는 뜻으로 문맥에 맞다. ③ 정확한 식별을 가리켜 옳다. ⑤ 말을 잃었다는 뜻으로 옳다.

passage: Madame Mallory came to the hospital not to explain the accident but to see for herself whether Hassan's hands still worked.
She learned they were undamaged, though he could not yet say the same about his feelings toward her.
She then offered him a pastry and asked what he tasted.
One by one, he named the almond, the apricot, the nutmeg, and finally the crushed vanilla folded into the puff pastry.
What his answer proved to her was that ______________________.
She left without saying much more, but something between them had already changed.
The accident that had briefly separated them ended up bringing them closer than either had expected.
choices: he had memorized her recipe book in advance
his sense of taste remained as extraordinary as ever
he no longer wished to work as a chef
French pastries were superior to Indian dishes
he had lost his ability to distinguish flavors
blank.explanation_ko: 손이 다치지 않았을 뿐 아니라 재료를 하나하나 정확히 맞히는 것을 보고, 그의 미각이 여전히 비범하다는 것을 확인했다는 흐름이므로 ②가 맞다.
blank.distractor_ko: ① 레시피를 외웠다는 근거가 없다. ③ 요리를 그만두고 싶어 한다는 서술은 없다. ④ 두 요리를 비교하지 않는다. ⑤ 미각을 잃었다는 것은 정확히 맞힌 것과 정반대다.

irrelevant.intro: Madame Mallory quietly entered Hassan's hospital room sometime after dinner and studied his bandaged hands as he slept.
sentences: When he opened his eyes, she offered a brief, unexplained apology and moved toward the rain-streaked window.
Hassan admitted he could not yet forgive her, even though he was relieved his hands were undamaged.
She then produced a package of almond and apricot pastries and asked what he could taste in them.
French hospitals generally require visitors to check in at the front desk before entering a patient's room.
His precise answer, naming even the crushed vanilla pods folded into the pastry, left her unable to speak.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: ④는 프랑스 병원의 방문 절차에 관한 일반적 사실로, Mallory 부인이 Hassan을 찾아가 화해하고 그의 미각을 확인하는 이 장면의 흐름과 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①은 사과와 반응, ②는 Hassan의 감정, ③은 페이스트리 시험의 시작, ⑤는 그 결과로 모두 흐름에 맞는다.

order.given: Madame Mallory quietly slipped into Hassan's hospital room and, after studying his bandaged hands, offered a brief apology.

blocks.A: Rain had begun to fall outside, and for a while neither of them spoke; Hassan finally asked her why she hated his family, but she only moved toward the window without answering.
blocks.B: She then took out a package of pastries and asked him to name what he tasted, and one by one he identified every hidden ingredient, down to the crushed vanilla pods.
blocks.C: Unable to find words, she placed the pastries on his tray, wished him well, and left; only then did Hassan realize how tense he had been in her presence.

order.explanation_ko: 사과 뒤 (A) 침묵과 질문이 창가 응시로 이어지고 → (B) 페이스트리를 꺼내 미각을 시험하는 장면 → (C) 말을 잃고 떠나는 결말 순서이므로 ①이다.
order.distractor_ko: (B)의 페이스트리 장면은 (A)의 창가 응시 뒤에 이어져야 자연스럽고, (C)의 "말을 잃었다"는 (B)의 정확한 답변 뒤에만 성립한다.

insert.insert_sentence: One by one, he named the nutmeg, the pistachio paste, and finally the crushed vanilla pods folded into the puff pastry.

passage_marked.text: Madame Mallory pulled a package of almond and apricot pastries from her basket and asked Hassan to try one.
"Tell me," she said, turning to look out the window, "what do you taste?"
He began simply, with apricot and almond filling, before she asked if there was anything else.
Madame Mallory could not find words; his answer had changed something in her.
When she finally turned around, her eyes glistened like Spanish olives.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 "One by one"은 앞서 간단히 답한 것(apricot and almond)에 이어 더 세부적인 재료를 하나씩 맞혀 가는 순서를 나타내므로, 간단한 답변 뒤 ③에 들어가야 한다.
insert.distractor_ko: ①②는 아직 미각 시험이 시작되기 전이라 이르고, ④⑤는 이미 그녀가 말을 잃은 뒤라 그 이후에 재료를 나열하는 것은 순서상 늦다.

passage: Madame Mallory visited Hassan in the hospital and apologized for the accident she had caused.
Though he could not yet forgive her, he was relieved that his hands were undamaged.
She then tested his palate with pastries, and he identified every ingredient with remarkable precision.
His answer left her speechless and changed something in how she viewed him.
The accident that had briefly divided them eventually gave way to an unlikely friendship.
Hassan went on to train under her, open his own restaurant in Paris, and blend French and Indian cuisine.
What began as a bitter rivalry ultimately blossomed into mutual respect and celebrated success.
summary.summary_template: Although the accident initially left Hassan and Madame Mallory __(A)__, his extraordinary sense of taste ultimately __(B)__ their rivalry into a lasting friendship and culinary partnership.
summary.explanation_ko: 사고로 소원해졌던(estranged) 두 사람이 Hassan의 뛰어난 미각으로 우정과 협력 관계로 바뀌었다(transformed)는 것이 글의 흐름이므로 ⑤가 맞다.
summary.distractor_ko: ①④ 사고 직후 관계를 reconciled·cooperative로 보는 것은 이르다. ②③ ignored·prolonged는 우정으로 발전한 결말과 어긋난다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그녀의 표정은 내가 절대 음감과 같은 요리 미각을 지녔다고 말해 주었다.
writing.answer: Her expression told me that I possessed the culinary equivalent of perfect pitch.
writing.explanation_ko: tell + 간접목적어 + that절 구조이며, the culinary equivalent of perfect pitch는 "절대 음감에 상당하는 요리적 재능"이라는 비유적 표현이다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오. (총 11단어)
writing.ko_prompt: 다음번에 당신이 다른 나라를 방문할 때, 그곳에서 면 요리 대신 그 나라 요리사의 이야기를 들어 보라.
conditions: The next time 으로 시작할 것
writing.answer: The next time you visit, listen to a local chef's story.
writing.explanation_ko: The next time 뒤에는 시간의 부사절이 이어지고, 시간의 부사절에서는 미래의 일이라도 현재시제(visit)를 쓴다.

writing.question: 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 넣어 문장을 완성하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그는 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 그의 감정은 뒤죽박죽이었다.
writing.template: He did not say anything. His emotions were ______ ______.
writing.explanation_ko: "감정이 뒤죽박죽이다"는 emotions were mixed up으로 쓴다. mix up은 "뒤섞다, 혼란스럽게 하다"라는 구동사다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Only after she was gone did I realize how incredibly tense I had been in her presence.
writing.answer: 그녀가 떠난 후에야 나는 그녀가 있을 때 내가 얼마나 극도로 긴장하고 있었는지 깨달았다.
writing.explanation_ko: Only after ~가 문장 앞에 나오면서 주어와 동사가 도치된 did I realize 구문이고, how incredibly tense I had been은 realize의 목적어 역할을 하는 간접의문문이다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: What started as a __(A)__ between two cultures blossomed into a beautiful friendship and mutual __(B)__ of cultures.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문은 두 문화 간의 불화(feud)로 시작된 것이 아름다운 우정과 문화에 대한 상호 이해(understanding)로 발전했다고 요약한다.

writing.question: 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: Hassan의 뛰어난 미각은 그가 두 문화를 조화시키고 독특한 요리를 만들도록 이끌었다.
writing.answer: Hassan's amazing sense of taste led him to harmonize the two cultures and create unique dishes.
writing.explanation_ko: lead + 목적어 + to부정사 구문으로, harmonize와 create가 to 뒤에서 병렬 연결된다.
